790570101.text: Hi! I'm the Acting Director of this attraction. Do you have any questions for me?

790570103.text: Whoa! The Water Droplet is speaking again! And its voice is slightly different...

790570105.text: Haha! Your reaction is exactly as I expected!

790570106.text: Don't be so surprised, and listen carefully. The sound is coming from the speaker by the wall.

790570107.text: I'm speaking to you via prerecorded lines... Anyway, it was Idy... Ah! I mean Daiya who prepared these lines in advance!

790570108.text: As for the specifics, you can talk to Engineer. His explanation will certainly be clearer and more comprehensive!

790570110.text: For some reason, it feels like anything is possible when we're in the miraculous Veluriyam Mirage...

790570112.text: That's a good question! It's because I don't think I'm the best candidate for the job...

790570113.text: My partners and I were all more or less influenced by Director Zosimos, and we're equals in terms of talent.

790570114.text: We're busy expanding our repertoire and polishing our skills.

790570115.text: My partners often present ideas to me, and sometimes, Fake Playwright goes over my head and just does things.

790570116.text: But as long as the majority supports it, and the show is good, then I'm happy too!

790570117.text: If one of the others becomes more capable than me and wishes to manage the project, I would immediately give up the position!

790570118.text: You're too humble. Shouldn't a director be more forceful? If you're always accommodating the opinions of others, it's bound to lead to arguments, isn't it?

790570141.text: Paimon was wondering about the decision behind using narration and dialogue to help guests imagine the scenes in the play!

790570142.text: About that... if I'm being honest... it's actually pretty simple...

790570146.text: Actually, everything you've experienced is a result of compromise.

790570147.text: I've only seen a few of Director Zosimos's films, so I have some hazy ideas. But we encountered great difficulty trying to realize them.

790570148.text: During planning, each scene only had a few lines, but many actors, props, and backdrops, all of which cost a lot.

790570149.text: In the words of Zosimos, money could solve any problem back in his homeland. But in Veluriyam Mirage, the only currency to spend is the labor hours of us Hydro Eidolons.

790570150.text: Consider the Black Nacre and the All-Devouring Kraken, for example. If we were to recreate a fully armed pirate ship, a huge mechanical sea monster, and even dig out a large expanse of water for the performance...

790570151.text: It would take millions, maybe even billions of Mora! If we convert it into working hours for us Hydro Eidolons, it would take months, even if we got all our friends to help!

790570152.text: Th-That much!? Paimon actually underestimated the cost!?

790570153.text: That's why we gave up on most backdrops and props and chose to focus our efforts on the Choo-Choo Cart and the final battle.

790570154.text: That way, we'd be able to give our audience a few unforgettable experiences, instead of everything being equally mediocre and forgettable.

790570155.text: That kinda makes sense. The Choo-Choo Cart in the Black Nacre was amazing. At the very least, it felt like a ship, and the final battle was pretty special.

790570156.text: Sounds like something we heard in Liyue... What was it again?

790570169.text: Well, I really want to introduce everyone in the troupe to you, but ever since Zosimos enlightened us, we've each been busy pursuing all sorts of knowledge.

790570170.text: Every one of them has formed a... unique personality now. It's really way too complicated to try and convey everything over the broadcast system.

790570171.text: Also, there's a lot of new words and voice lines that Engineer hasn't finished working on yet.

790570172.text: So, I can't explain things with recordings yet. You'll have to speak to them yourselves.

790570173.text: Hold on! Paimon needs some time to digest all of that! Did Paimon hear something about another Water Droplet?

790570176.text: (The director seems to be gesturing and acting out something, but it's almost impossible to figure out...)

790570177.text: Looks like there's nothing we can do. Director Water Droplet doesn't have the ability to talk about that topic!

790570178.text: Let's do what it said and speak to the others.

790570179.text: If we get a chance, we should ask Engineer about the voice lines the director mentioned.

790570181.text: How polite of you! If you have any questions about the show, feel free to ask me!

790570201.text: Hi, esteemed audience members! I'm Fake Playwright, one of the staff working on Three-Day Reverie. Can I help you with anything?

790570203.text: That's a good question! It seems I have some explaining to do.

790570204.text: Long story short, if I can't write anything appropriate soon, I'll be fired!

790570205.text: Whoa! Is it that bad? You make it sound like... Water Droplets have strict rules too!

790570241.text: I told you, I'm just one of the staff. It's like you're mocking me when you address me like that...

790570242.text: #Hey! Aren't you being a little too sensitive? That's not what {NICKNAME} meant! {M#He}{F#She} is always sincere!

790570243.text: Forgive me, being sensitive is something that comes naturally to us artistically gifted playwrights...

790570244.text: According to Mr. Zosimos, sometimes people in the industry have been misunderstood or even ruthlessly attacked because they were careless with their wording...

790570245.text: While such a demanding audience may not appear in the Veluriyam Mirage...

790570246.text: Mr. Zosimos also said that whenever we create something, we must be prepared to receive the attention of a larger audience and never leave it up to luck!

790570247.text: Hmm, we may have gone off topic a bit. Though those are more my own personal expectations, you could also consider them suggestions.

790570248.text: Those expectations are way too strict! Are you going to quibble over every single little word?

790570249.text: So if we create a show based on our own experiences, like the story of the Anemo Archon and Dvalin...

790570250.text: Would people come forward just to fuss over things like... Hmm, something like "How disrespectful! How dare you make the Anemo Archon seem so carefree! That's far too presumptuous!"

790570266.text: Daiya's voice said that we should talk to you and tell interesting stories that will help with your script writing!

790570267.text: Oh... So Chief Director heard about your adventures from Idyia. Yes, your assistance is necessary...

790570268.text: But as you can see, the process of writing a script is very long. I'm worried that your stories will be so rich and detailed that I will fail to remember them after a time.

790570269.text: Please use the device in front of me to make a recording. That way I can review it whenever I want!

790570270.text: #We're experts at that! {NICKNAME}, Paimon will allow you to decide what kind of material we should provide to Daiya's Three-Day Reverie!

790570271.text: After a short discussion with Paimon, you select some of the most outlandish things you've encountered in your journey and the stories from several novels before recording them in a concise and easy-to-understand tone for Fake Playwright...

790570272.text: Wow! That's such a long recording! This is more material than I ever expected!

790570273.text: I shall specially write a line to extol the great deed you have performed here today in sharing your stories!

790570274.text: Hehe, Paimon wonders what kind of show this super professional Water Droplet will turn our stories into!

790570277.text: Right! We're only here to observe! We'll leave you to it then!

790570278.text: You're so polite and careful with your words! I hope you have a pleasant visit!

790570301.text: *panting* You two sure are full of energy. Unfortunately, I don't have time to entertain you...

790570303.text: That panting sounds so realistic! It's Paimon's first time hearing a Water Droplet sound tired. Paimon never realized this is what a worn-out Water Droplet would be like...

790570335.text: Well, guess it can't be helped. That's what you call an "occupational hazard."

790570304.text: Technical maintenance? Quite the specialized term to pop out of nowhere...

790570334.text: I appreciate the concern. I'll take a break once I'm done here... But will there ever come a day when my work is truly done...?

790570401.text: Oho! Two special guests! Is there anything I can do for you? I'm Loafer, and I specialize in the lowest-effort solutions...

790570403.text: Yeah, Paimon would like to know too!

790570404.text: Did you get that name because you never do any work?

790570405.text: Heh! It's not like that! Whether it's controlling the play's progress or making the necessary props and scene elements, I've always completed my work on time!

790570406.text: Loafing is a state of mind. It strives to achieve the most with the least effort.

790570407.text: For example, instead of making something three-dimensional, only the front and back of a scene element is prepared. So, uh... In the words of Chief Director, it saves us a lot of time!

790570410.text: Doesn't that mean it has no sides?

790570411.text: Isn't tricking the audience's eyes all we need to do?

790570412.text: For example, slowing down the Choo-Choo Cart right in front of a scene element, and then shooting off right when it's about to move past it.

790570413.text: Doing that will keep most of the audience's focus on the front of the scene element! Think about, didn't you do the same with the sea monster's minions?

790570414.text: Otherwise, our troupe wouldn't have time to complete the more important scenes.

790570415.text: Instead of wasting time focusing on the "sides of the sea monster's minions," the completeness of the entire experience is definitely more important.

790570417.text: From what you said... calling you "Loafer" is a kind of compliment?

790570428.text: Thank you so much! Your wisdom lights up my day! Come again when you're free!

790570501.text: Work! Work! Work! Sprint to the finish! Go above and beyond the call of duty, win early!

790570503.text: When one task is done, I can start another! I will go wherever the need is greatest!

790570504.text: It's just a little Water Droplet, but it's got such a scary aura...

790570505.text: It seems absolutely in love with working. Just getting close to it feels like Paimon will be dragged along to work with it... forever...

790570506.text: Huh? Did I just hear you talking about me?

790570507.text: No, we never did anything of the sort! We're busy people too, so we'll be on our way...

790570508.text: Oooooh! Busy? You're really busy? How about you give some of your work to me?

790570511.text: I'll take any job! Anything! And I can learn if I lack the know-how! I love challenging new jobs!

790570512.text: Did we misunderstand this Water Droplet? Instead of dragging others along to suffer with it, it actually does their work for them?

790570513.text: Um... So, Water Droplet, what work do you usually do?

790570514.text: Let me think... I don't think I have any fixed responsibilities.

790570515.text: Chief Director asks for my help with controlling the show's mechanisms, Fake Playwright makes me run errands and carry reference books for the script writing...

790570516.text: Engineer sends me to clean the rails, and Loafer has asked for my help making props.

790570528.text: Alright... Paimon's kinda curious about what it's working on, but let's not disturb it...

790570601.text: (It seems to be the Hydro Eidolon from before that was operating some mechanisms according to the Chief Director's instructions.)

790570602.text: (But without a console of its own, it is incapable of speaking. It just constantly trembles with fear as if it has done something wrong...)

790570701.text: (A Hydro Eidolon that seems to be up to something in the corner. According to Chief Director, its nickname is "Food Manager.")

790570702.text: (But... isn't that a bit strange? What do Hydro Eidolons even eat? Or maybe... it's responsible for feeding those ghost mechanisms?)
